findings.title: The failed-diff-fetch path is unspecified — a silent total loss of the diff can still produce a clean PASS
findings.description: Description: D2 establishes the invariant "`diff_injection` is `None` when `inputs` has no `diff` key … When a diff was part of the review, the key is always written", and D3 defines the recording for the one silent-loss path it found (`_add_injection` returning `False`). But the other silent-loss path is not specified: `_run_git_diff` returns `None` on git failure (`_logger.warning` + `return None`), which means `_add_injection` is never called. D2 forces the implementer to produce a `DiffInjection` anyway (the key exists), and the design does not say what values it carries. The natural implementation — `DiffInjection(total_chars=0, injected_chars=0)` — records `truncated == False`, so Part B never fires and the artifact reads as "saw it all". This is reachable in practice: `_run_git_diff_filenames` (`--name-only`) and `_run_git_diff` (full diff) are separate invocations, and a repository with a misconfigured external diff driver or textconv filter fails the body fetch while the name-only call succeeds — so `EmptyDiffError`'s pre-flight guard does not cover it. The requirement this leaves unmet is the slice's own Value claim: "After this slice a PASS means the model either saw the whole diff or read files with its tools." The fix is one sentence in D3: a `None` return from the body fetch records the same truncation-to-zero shape D3 already defines for the budget-skip case (which then makes Part B fire correctly on it).

findings.title: All three parts the slice-plan entry assigns are delivered, with the plan's open decisions each resolved and justified
findings.description: Description: The plan entry (900 #927) requires: Part A with "design picks the minimum that lets a gate decide" (D1/D2 pick the boolean + counts in header/JSON — the minimum a gate needs); Part B with "design picks between forcing CONCERNS with a synthetic finding and failing the run" (D4 picks CONCERNS, with the #5-precedent argument made explicitly); Part C with "design must decide what counts as 'differs' … so an alias resolving to its own snapshot is not reported as a substitution" (D9). Both paths (CLI and pipeline) are covered structurally by riding `ReviewResult` through the shared `run_review_with_profile`. The plan's exclusions (defaults, #114) are honored, and diff ordering/`--stat` were conditional scope ("in scope only if design shows it is small") that the design deferred to #137 per the plan's own fallback instruction.

findings.title: The design's load-bearing factual claims about the codebase are accurate
findings.description: Description: Verified against source: `_truncate` truncates at `max_file_size` and warns only; the diff-injection call site discards `_add_injection`'s boolean return, so the total-limit skip is real and silent; `builders/code.py` imports `_truncate` (keeping its signature is necessary); `persistence.py`'s render is exactly the `if findings / elif fallback_used / elif degraded` chain D6 claims, so a synthetic finding would hide the not-parsed notice without D6's fix; `VerdictSource` is a closed two-member enum whose docstring's stated concern is open reason strings, not member count; `_stamp_tool_telemetry` stamps before its tools early-return exactly as D8 assumes; the OpenAI `metadata["model"]` stamp carries the requested id; and `metrology/identity.py` keys judge identity on `aiModel` (line 35), making D10's metrology consequence real and correctly disclosed.

findings.title: Proportionality holds — no scope creep, and weight matches the plan's 3/5 effort
findings.description: Description: Every mechanism traces to a plan requirement: D11/D13 exist because Part C must define behavior when a provider reports nothing; D12 covers the multi-model case the #92 recovery turn makes possible; D6 is required for Part B's own correctness. The two new modules (`review/coverage.py`, `models/snapshot.py`) are each a single pure function placed at the correct layer, and `_truncate`'s signature is deliberately preserved rather than refactored. Nothing restates other documents, and no abstraction is introduced that nothing uses.

findings.title: `aiModel`'s meaning change is disclosed but carries a cross-repo consequence the design handles by disclosure rather than a coordination step
findings.description: Description: Changing the value domain of an existing externally-read frontmatter key is a stronger contract change than adding one; slice 919's precedent required a context-forge coordination step for its `verdictSource` addition. Here the design's argument is defensible — in-repo the only reader is `metrology/identity.py` (verified), the change makes `aiModel` mean what consumers assumed, and the one visible consequence (metrology identity shift for dated snapshots) is stated explicitly. Worth confirming CF/Amoeba consumers of `aiModel` accept dated ids, but nothing gates on it today per the design's grep.
